| [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) v2 | For a system driven without feedback, the work dissipated equals the memory that fails to predict the drive, so only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; once actions feed back, prediction is no longer what efficiency requires | Still, Sivak, Bell & Crooks (2012), [LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md): β⟨W_diss⟩ for the step x_t → x_{t+1} equals I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] (Eq. 14, an identity). The summed nostalgia lower-bounds dissipation and adds to Landauer's bound (Eq. 21). Fiderer et al. ([LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md)) show that with feedback, predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents can be disjoint. The claim is an ensemble average, not a per-operation floor. It needs a Markov drive to be nonnegative, and the prediction-is-necessary slogan fails under feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v2 | Landauer's principle prices only logically irreversible steps, and prices them in exported entropy rather than heat, so acquiring, copying or evaluating a bit, and learning it, carry no minimum thermodynamic cost | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state (erasure, merging of control flow), and it is at least k ln 2 of entropy exported per bit, which "need not" be heat. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) and Still et al. ([LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md)) agree. Information learnt is bounded by entropy production and can be paid almost entirely in weight entropy. The only per-bit heat term is Landauer's, on entropy removed. The synthesis across the three is the record's. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) | Organisms differ from dissipative structures such as a candle flame not by far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance, nor by circular self-maintenance alone, but by organisational differentiation: several distinct constraints that produce one another at different time scales | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-099.md) | Tryptophan networks in microtubule architectures support collective superradiant excitonic states, and their thermal quantum yield rises with network size and survives static disorder of room-temperature size | Babcock et al. (2024), [LIT-645](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-645.md): a radiative Hamiltonian of up to more than 10⁵ tryptophan transition dipoles, on tubulin geometry, predicts superradiant states up to about 4000 times the single-tryptophan rate in a centriole, and a thermal quantum yield that rises with network size and is almost unaffected by static disorder of about 200 cm⁻¹, though that disorder cuts the brightest state's enhancement from about 3600 to about 20. This is not evidence for Orch OR or for any claim about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md) | After mass bleaching, coral recovery on a reef crest depends on large herbivorous fishes keeping macroalgae down, because recovery runs through recruitment and survival that macroalgae suppress, not through the persistence of surviving colonies alone | Hughes et al. (2007), [LIT-711](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md). On the reef crest at Orpheus Island after the 1998 bleaching, four roofless cages kept large and medium fishes out of 25 m² plots for 30 months. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover inside against 4.1% and 1.7% in controls. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%, with recruitment about two-thirds lower and mortality of established colonies more than double. Control recovery came mainly from recruits of taxa bleaching had removed. Proposed: one site, four replicates, plot scale, and fish exclusion standing in for herbivore exclusion. The algal state vanished within 30 days of reopening. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-129.md) | In Acropora millepora the natural night-light regime is necessary for spawning on the expected night, and displacing it delays or abolishes both release and a spawning-night programme of G-protein-coupled signalling genes | Kaniewska et al. In 2011, colonies under natural night light spawned with the reef, while colonies lit after sunset or kept dark for the preceding week did not spawn that night (N = 6, 5, 5). 184 transcripts changed around release in ambient colonies, early in lit ones and not at all in dark ones, and the induced genes were enriched for G-protein-coupled signalling. In 2006, blue, green or white nocturnal light delayed spawning 6–8 h or two nights and red did not. Proposed: one species and site, small groups, and a cascade inferred from co-expression. | [THEORY-130](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-130.md) | Coral bleaching is the breakdown of a regulated host–symbiont exchange, reached by more than one route, not a single mechanism of symbiont loss | Two reviews, with no data of their own. | [THEORY-135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-135.md) | Multicellular cooperation depends on suppressing cells that gain fitness at the expense of the organism, across five foundations (proliferation inhibition, controlled cell death, division of labour, resource allocation and maintenance of the extracellular environment); cancer-like cheating on them is found across the independent origins of complex multicellularity, so complex multicellularity can be understood as a system for detecting and suppressing cheaters | Aktipis et al. | [THEORY-160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md) | In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators | Baez (2020), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md), read in [NOTE-630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-630.md), Theorems 3, 4, 8 and 10, with Alfsen and Shultz's theorem quoted as Theorem 12. | [THEORY-178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md) | Transcriptional regulation alone can make a bacterium's gene-expression state depend on its history: a transient change to one regulator can leave its regulatory network in a different self-maintaining state, but only through a gene that reaches a positive circuit | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md). | [THEORY-179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-179.md) | In genetically identical E. coli, a cell's swarming potential is a transient inherited state: its descendants share it for about four generations and lose it by about seven, and it tracks the cell's iron status rather than a bistable switch | Bhattacharyya et al. | [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) v3 | Mehta and Schwab's correspondence between Kadanoff's variational renormalization group and restricted Boltzmann machines is an identity of parametrizations, under which an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution; away from that point it does not make training by distribution fitting a renormalization | Mehta and Schwab (2014), [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md), Eqs. 18–22: setting the RG kernel T = −E + H makes the RG coarse Hamiltonian equal the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for every parameter value, and Kadanoff's exactness condition equal to zero KL divergence. | [THEORY-202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md) | In variational renormalization, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a stated target | Lin and Tegmark (2016), [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md), arXiv v1–v2 appendix, a part dropped from the journal text: a family of joint Hamiltonians with Z_tot = Z and the wrong marginal, and the remark that any non-interacting pair meets the trace condition. | [THEORY-205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-205.md) | For a short-range lattice model on a cylinder, with block and environment as slabs separated by a buffer, the information-bottleneck encoder at its first transition depends on the block only through the boundary weak value of the leading transfer-matrix eigenvector, at β_c = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B): at large circumference this is the lowest-dimension primary, so the first feature information-theoretic relevance selects is the most RG-relevant operator; nothing is shown for blocks inside a buffer shell or for the fixed-alphabet RSMI optimum | Gordon, Banerjee, Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2020), [LIT-885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-885.md), Eqs. 3–5 and B2–C11, with one numerical check on a three-site critical Ising cylinder, reproduced exactly in [NOTE-690](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-690.md). | [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v2 | Directional information measures between two symmetrically coupled units follow the path of a recorded drive, not the symmetry of the coupling: flow reads two-way under moderate drive of one unit and one-way under strong drive | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). | [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md) | For a non-normal linear operator the eigenvalues govern only the long-run limit: a system whose every mode decays can amplify perturbations over finite times, and hold more forced variance, by factors its spectrum does not predict | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. | [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md) | Time dependence can destabilize a non-normal linear system that is stable at every instant; non-normality is necessary for this, and random variation of the operator destabilizes generically, needing less variation the more non-normal and less damped the mean operator | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). | [THEORY-408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md) | In a one-locus model with non-overlapping generations, random mating and weak selection, gene frequencies change as if each individual maximized its inclusive fitness, so a trait that costs its bearer spreads only if its effect on relatives exceeds 1/r times the cost; the increase of mean inclusive fitness is proved only for traits whose total effect on others is not negative | Hamilton (1964), Part I, [LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md), read in full in [NOTE-401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-401.md). Each effect an individual causes falls partly on genes identical by descent with its own (weight r) and partly on others, which only dilute. So selection tracks inclusive fitness. The threshold is written −k > 1/r (§5), not rb > c: "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins". The maximization theorem needs non-negative total effects on others; for harming traits the change only points uphill. r is exact only for loci not under selection, and Hamilton could not bound the error (§4). | Active |
| [THEORY-431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) | For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects | Crooks (1999), [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md), read in [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md), with Jarzynski (1997), [LIT-517](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) ([NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md)), and Seifert's review (2012), [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md)). The work equality ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} holds at any switching rate, and Crooks derives it from a trajectory-level entropy-production theorem; Seifert derives every known theorem of the kind from one master theorem. These are exact given their premises. They are not proofs of the second law, since the dynamics build irreversibility in, and they say nothing about extremum principles for steady states. Their practical reach is work fluctuations of order k_BT. | Active |
| [THEORY-463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md) | In classical statistical mechanics a strictly irreversible approach to equilibrium cannot come from the isolated Hamiltonian dynamics alone: the fine-grained Gibbs entropy is constant and bounded systems recur, so each account surveyed either weakens the target to typical or long-run behaviour or adds something from outside the dynamics | Frigg & Werndl (2023), [LIT-114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), the SEP entry, read in [NOTE-103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md). The impossibility half rests on standard consequences of Liouville's theorem, time-reversal invariance and Poincaré recurrence. The classification half is the survey's: it is stated account by account, not argued as a general result. The entry is classical only, excludes the direction of time, and reports rather than settles the disputes about each repair. | Active |
| [THEORY-466](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md) | Among contestants of equal prowess with dangerous weapons, individual selection can favour conventional fighting backed by retaliation: an escalating Hawk is not evolutionarily stable, Retaliator is at most neutrally stable because Mouse ties it, and in a contest settled by persistence alone no fixed persistence is stable while an exponential mixture is | Maynard Smith & Price (1973), [LIT-505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md), read in full in [NOTE-404](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-404.md). The paper calls Retaliator an ESS "though Mouse does equally well", which fails its own second condition. There is no Hawk–Dove game, no "dove", no difference in prowess and no ownership, so it is not the source of display, deference or owner–intruder conventions. | Active |
| [THEORY-473](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md) | Scaled down to one organism, Hutchinson's niche, defined as the conditions that give that individual an expected lifetime reproductive success of at least one, is observed only as a point; the rest of it is counterfactual, reached by translocation in only a few dimensions and otherwise inferred from other individuals, so in practice it is the niche of a phenotype class, and its authors call it mostly metaphorical | Takola & Schielzeth (2022), [LIT-127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md), read in full in [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md). The working definition (p. 5) gives the individualized niche an absolute-fitness boundary, expected LRS ≥ 1, and splits it into realized, potential, time-slice, prospective and trajectory-based niches. That the realized niche is a point and the potential niche unobservable follows from the definitions. The paper concedes there is "no empirical solution" at the individual level (p. 15), and its fix, marginalizing fitness functions across individuals, is schematic. It is a framework for structuring research, by its authors' own account, not a measurement. | Active |
| [THEORY-499](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md) | The breakup of the Eulalia parent body beside the Jupiter 3:1 resonance, 785–965 Myr ago, can plausibly have supplied the cluster of large lunar craters dated near 800 Ma, but only in the most favourable of five model solutions, with an average largest lunar impactor too small for Copernicus, and with the cluster's absolute date inherited from Copernicus alone | Bottke, Vokrouhlický, Dykhuis & Zellner (2026), [LIT-009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-009.md), read in full in [NOTE-002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-002.md). A chain of multiplied factors (family fit, J3:1 influx, WISE incompleteness, collisional loss, impact probabilities) gives, for Solution 5 only, about 7,000 D ≥ 2 km fragments into the resonance and a largest expected lunar impactor of ">3 km". A Monte Carlo puts the seven ~800 Ma craters "generally" within 1σ. It is an existence argument, not an estimate: one factor is tuned by eye, only the most favourable solution is propagated, and the seven craters are dated by N(1) against one sample-dated crater. The Earth, Mars and Venus links are the authors' own speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-508](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-508.md) | The Belousov–Zhabotinsky oscillation is a relaxation cycle in which autocatalytic production of HBrO₂ oxidizes the catalyst until bromide, released as the oxidized catalyst is reduced by bromomalonic acid, switches the autocatalysis off; a closed batch oscillates only as a transient of up to several thousand cycles on its way to equilibrium, and only a continuous-flow reactor sustains it indefinitely | Zhabotinsky (2007), [LIT-531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-531.md), the Scholarpedia review by one of the reaction's eponyms, read in full in [NOTE-414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-414.md). The mechanism is supported by the primary kinetics and by phase-resetting with injected Br⁻, Ag⁺ and Ce⁴⁺. The closed/open distinction matters for any use of BZ as a dissipative structure: a closed batch is a long transient, and only a fed reactor holds it away from equilibrium. The Oregonator models oscillation and excitability qualitatively, not quantitatively. The "several thousand cycles" figure is uncited, and the primary papers were not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises the Earth's entropy production, chiefly by increasing the absorption of sunlight, and if the planet is held at maximum entropy production, the negative feedbacks of that state would give the homeostasis the Gaia hypothesis postulates | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). | [THEORY-543](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md) | Diffusion can destabilise a homogeneous steady state of reacting chemicals that is stable without it: a disturbance of one finite wave-length grows while uniform and very short ones decay, so a stationary pattern appears whose spacing is set by the reaction and diffusion constants and only its phase by the disturbance; with two substances this needs them to diffuse at different rates, and the pattern lasts only while free energy is supplied | Turing (1952), [LIT-535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), read in full in [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). | [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | In REST2 replica-exchange simulations of intrinsically disordered proteins, high swap acceptance and short round trips show that replicas mix along the temperature ladder, not that conformations are sampled, because the upper rungs collapse the chain; sampling shows only when independent demultiplexed replicas agree in their structural distributions | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). A how-to chapter whose one load-bearing methodological point is that high swap acceptance "is not, in isolation, sufficient evidence of robust conformational sampling or convergence" (p. 18). The reason the reading draws out is that REST2's upper rungs are unphysical Hamiltonians on which disordered chains over-collapse, so replicas can swap freely without the chain rearranging. The chapter argues this and shows a passing example; it shows no failed run, and its convergence criteria have no quantitative threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-567](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md) | In the donation game, where a cooperator pays c for another to get b, defectors win in a well-mixed population, and each of five mechanisms makes cooperators evolutionarily stable above a benefit-to-cost threshold: kin selection r > c/b, direct reciprocity w > c/b, indirect reciprocity q > c/b, network reciprocity b/c > k and group selection b/c > 1 + n/m; the rules cover altruism only, not mutualism, coordination or conflict | Nowak (2006), [LIT-501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-501.md), read in [NOTE-409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-409.md), main text only. A four-page review that casts each known mechanism as a 2×2 game so that one set of criteria applies to all. The five ESS conditions are confirmed by the main text; the derivations are in the supporting material, which was not read, and in cited papers. Several rules hold only under weak selection, regular graphs or rare group splitting. Every mechanism is modelled with the donation game, so mutualism, coordination and conflict are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-634](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-634.md) | In a ring of M chemotactic catalyst species, each making the next one's substrate, the non-reciprocal nearest-neighbour coupling makes the linear stability matrix circulant: the uniform state goes unstable for any M exactly when the species attract themselves, and the parity of M then decides the leading mode, a real alternating mode for even M that sorts species by parity into two static clusters, and a complex pair for odd M that can give persistent oscillation | Ouazan-Reboul, Agudo-Canalejo & Golestanian (2023), [LIT-036](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-036.md), read in [NOTE-079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-079.md). The spectrum is exact for equal parameters (Eq. 5): instability iff μ(p) − μ(s) < 0, real leading eigenvalue for M = 2K, complex pair for M = 2K + 1. Brownian dynamics at M = 5 and 6 bear out the linear predictions; the odd-cycle oscillation is one trajectory at one parameter set. Direct metabolic partners repel; same-parity second neighbours co-aggregate. The origin-of-life reading is untested, and the authors concede in the review file that real catalysts' mobilities are unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) | Social behaviour evolves as if each individual valued a neighbour's fitness against its own by their coefficient of relationship, and its discriminations evolve to make that coefficient determinate; so kin are favoured and strangers met with hostility, relatives fight less, and haplodiploid sisters, related by 3/4, are predisposed to worker altruism | Hamilton (1964), Part II, [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), read in full in [NOTE-410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-410.md), on Part I's model ([LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)). Two general principles, offered as an "unrigorous" generalization, are applied to alarm calls, kin recognition in gulls and terns, clones and colonies, Hymenoptera, and fights. The evidence is anecdotal. The author calls his positive indications for distant relatives "rather few and feeble", reports Australian halictines and multiple mating as running against the hymenopteran hypothesis, and explains anomalies case by case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-660.md) | The local branching geometry of physical tree networks, neurons, blood vessels, trees, corals and plants, is set by minimising the surface area of tubes that must keep a minimum circumference, not by minimising length: this predicts trifurcations once links are thick relative to their separation (χ = w/r above about 0.83) and orthogonal sprouts once one branch is much thinner than the other two (ρ = w′/w below about 0.6), both departures from Steiner trees that the data show qualitatively | Meng, Piazza, Both, Barzel & Barabási (2026), [LIT-069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), read in full with the SI in [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md). Only two symmetric motifs are solved, each by a local, penalised optimiser started from the Steiner layout; the "exact" mapping to string worldsheets holds for a problem the paper does not solve. The random-terminal prediction is a sigmoid fitted to one tetrahedron, trifurcations are partly made by a merging rule, the one robustness check moves the key statistic 4.3-fold, and the sprouting breakpoints are chosen per dataset with no null. Real motifs are about 25% longer than Steiner, which the model leaves unexplained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Altruism between non-relatives can be selected when each act costs the giver less than it benefits the recipient, the same partners meet often and symmetrically, and help is withheld from those who do not return it; in humans, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy and guilt are adaptations that regulate such exchange, and selection then favours sham versions of each and the ability to detect them | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). A verbal model, with a Prisoner's Dilemma sketch Hamilton communicated, followed by a functional account of the human emotions that would regulate reciprocity. The model is plausible and was later formalized. The psychology is fitted to 1960s social-psychology findings, mostly on American students, and the heritability of the dispositions is assumed. Trivers knows "of no psychological studies on the detection of sham moralistic aggression and sham guilt" (p. 51). His "unfairness" is inequity in exchange, not the division of a disputed resource. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md) | In the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with a probability w of meeting again, no strategy does better against an established TIT FOR TAT than TIT FOR TAT does against itself if and only if w ≥ (T−R)/(T−P) and w ≥ (T−R)/(R−S); always defecting is stable for every w, a cluster of reciprocators can invade it, and a nice stable strategy resists clusters, but the stability is only neutral, since always cooperating ties | Axelrod & Hamilton (1981), [LIT-498](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-498.md), read in full in [NOTE-411](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-411.md). Against TIT FOR TAT the best reply is always-defect or alternation, which gives the condition on w. The cluster result and the "ratchet" are explicit payoff comparisons. "Evolutionarily stable" here means no mutant does better, which is weaker than Maynard Smith and Price's definition: always cooperate does exactly as well. The model is deterministic and error-free. Tournament robustness is a separate, empirical claim about the strategies people submitted. | Active |
| [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) | For dynamics obeying detailed balance in a heat bath, the heat released in a transition between observer-defined macrostates is bounded below by the log-odds against its reversal less the internal entropy change; where a replicator's likeliest way back is a copy decaying within one generation, the bound grows with the copy's durability and the speed of copying, not with the information copied | England (2012; J. Chem. Phys. 2013), [LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md), read in [NOTE-419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-419.md). The general bound, β⟨ΔQ⟩ + ln π(II→I) + ΔS_int ≥ 0, is a coarse-grained second law and was re-derived. Applied to replication it gives a heat cost of about 2n ln(n τ_decay/τ_div) per copy, which falls away as division slows. The numbers for E. coli (within a factor of three of the bound) and RNA rest on an upper bound on the reverse probability that is argued from biology, not proved, and on an internal-entropy term set "arbitrarily". It prices finite-time irreversibility, not information, and draws no line between living and non-living replicators. | Active |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | The time-average of a single threshold (Hill) response to a periodic signal is independent of the signal's period for a fixed waveform, so a frequency cannot be read by one sigmoidal stage; two cascaded stages can read it, because the first changes the waveform with period; and a delayed kinesin–dynein signalling loop whose period grows with axon length, read out this way and coupled to protrusion and contraction, can hold an axon at a stable length | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
